cards.ex: Let me check and get back to you tomorrow.
I don't feel like cooking tonight.
Sorry, I can't make it on Friday.
He's really into cycling these days.
Let's circle back on this next week.

quiz.q: Let me check the numbers and ___ tomorrow.
quiz.note: get back to + 사람 순서로 씁니다.

quiz.q: Sorry, I can't ___ to dinner on Friday.
quiz.note: 약속에 못 간다고 할 때 쓰는 표현입니다.
be into = 관심이 많다, 빠져 있다.

quiz.q: Let's ___ on this after the holiday.

cards.ex: I'll touch base with you before the meeting.
I'll loop in the design team.
Just giving you a heads-up — I'll be late.
I'm totally worn out after this week.
I didn't like the song at first, but it's growing on me.

quiz.q: I'll ___ with you before the meeting.
Could you ___ Jenny ___ on this thread?
Thanks for the ___ about the delay.
quiz.note: 명사로 쓸 때 heads-up, 하이픈까지 함께 외워두세요.

quiz.q: I'm completely ___ after three classes today.
quiz.note: worn out = 기운이 다 빠진 상태.
처음엔 별로였는데 점점 좋아질 때 씁니다.

cards.ex: Drop me a line when you get there.
We don't have a plan — let's play it by ear.
That project is on the back burner for now.
I have mixed feelings about moving abroad.
Something feels off, but I can't put my finger on it.

quiz.q: ___ when you get to the hotel.
quiz.note: line은 '짧은 메모 한 줄'에서 온 표현입니다.
악보 없이 귀로 듣고 연주하던 데서 온 표현입니다.

quiz.q: That plan is ___ until next quarter.
quiz.note: 약한 불(뒷쪽 화구)에 올려둔다는 뜻에서 왔습니다.
좋기도 하고 아쉽기도 할 때 씁니다.
지도 위를 손가락으로 짚듯, 정확히 짚어낸다는 뜻입니다.
